# 2024 Annual Budget Review

## Summary
I sat down with the December bank statements over a pot of coffee and worked through the whole year. My savings rate landed at 22% of take-home pay, a little short of the 25% I sketched in January but still respectable for a year with a boiler replacement. Income stayed flat apart from a small bonus in March. I paid myself first each month, moving money into savings on the first working day, and that habit carried the year more than any clever spreadsheet did. Fixed costs were the part I underestimated most when I set the plan.

## Expenses
Rent took 34% of income, the largest single line and the one I watch hardest. Groceries averaged 410 EUR a month, above my 350 EUR target, because I shopped small and often during the autumn instead of doing one big Saturday run. The holiday fund overspent badly: I budgeted 1200 EUR for the summer trip and spent closer to 1900 EUR once trains, food and a rental car were added up. Utilities rose after the new boiler went in, roughly 80 EUR a month more from October. Insurance, phone and subscriptions all stayed close to plan. I also bought a winter coat for 240 EUR that I had not budgeted for, though it should last several seasons.

## Next Year
For next year I want to hold rent at the same share if the lease allows it. Groceries get a firm 380 EUR ceiling, and I will batch shop on Saturdays rather than popping out mid-week. The holiday fund gets a larger monthly transfer so I am not scraping money together in June. I also want one no-spend month in February to reset the habit.
